key_insight: ECHO uses output-entropy feedback to dynamically adjust replay-gradient weighting and mitigate catastrophic forgetting during LLM supervised fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: The approach may help preserve general capabilities when adapting engineering language models, but the abstract reports no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: Use KL-divergence decomposition to motivate output entropy as an online proxy for forgetting risk.
Measure deviations from the pre-trained model’s entropic equilibrium without reference-model inference.
Apply proportional feedback to dynamically modulate replay-data gradient weight.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on 0.6B–9B parameter architectures reportedly match or extend the observed plasticity–stability frontier in several comparisons and remain robust across varying data-mixing ratios.
watch_item: Entropy is a proxy rather than a direct measure of retained knowledge; its reliability and controller tuning require validation for each target domain.
paper_title: Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization: Pre-empting Catastrophic Forgetting via Dynamic Feedback
